en.headline: Police arrest man over 23,000 fraudulent customer-service calls
en.dek: A 24-year-old man was held after officers found a SIM-box modem that placed more than 23,000 scam calls in a week, with one victim losing over HK$100,000.
body: Police said they arrested a 24-year-old man on suspicion of operating a call centre that made more than 23,000 fraudulent calls in just over a week by impersonating online shopping platform customer-service staff.

Senior Inspector Liu Long-kwan of the Commercial Crime Bureau said the syndicate told victims there were problems with goods they had purchased and that the items needed to be returned or refunded. Callers then demanded deposits, handling fees or warned of large annual bank charges before directing transfers to accounts they controlled.

Officers raided a residential flat in Tseung Kwan O on 9 October and found a multi-port SIM-box modem still running, along with multiple phone cards, a computer, a tablet and handsets. The man had applied for a large number of post-paid SIM cards under a company name. At least one victim lost more than HK$100,000.
Police said the investigation is continuing.

zh.headline: 警拘24歲男涉逾2.3萬通假冒客服電話騙案
zh.dek: 警方在將軍澳住宅單位發現仍在運作的SIM卡數據機，一週內撥出逾2.3萬通詐騙電話，至少一名受害人損失逾10萬元。
body: 警方表示，拕捕一名24歲男子，涉嫌操控電話中心，在一週多內以假冒網上購物平台客服人員身份撥出超過2.3萬通詐騙電話。
商業罪案調查科高級督察廖龍坤說，集團向受害人聲稱已購商品有問題需要退貨或退款，然後以收取按金、手續費，或警告銀行戶口將被收取高昂年費等借口，要求受害人轉帳至其提供的戶口。
人員於10月9日在將軍澳一個住宅單位採取行動，發現一個多端口SIM卡數據機仍在運作，並檢獲多張電話卡、電腦、平板電腦及手機。該男子以公司名義申請大量後付費SIM卡。至少一名受害人損失超過10萬港元。
